title: Vijay's Last Film Has Been Waiting Five Months for a Censor Certificate. Ticket Platforms Just Listed It for June 19.
excerpt: Jana Nayagan was supposed to release on January 9. Then the CBFC withheld the certificate. Then the entire film leaked online. Now June 19 — three days before the Chief Minister's birthday — appears to be the target.
body:
The saga of *Jana Nayagan* — Thalapathy Vijay's final film before he became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu — just took another turn. Ticket booking platforms BookMyShow and District by Zomato have both listed June 19, 2026 as the release date. Fans noticed. Social media noticed. The producers have not confirmed.

Here's what makes this more interesting than a standard release date story: the film has been sitting without a censor certificate for five months, it was pirated and leaked online in full HD in April, and the man who stars in it now runs the state government.

## The Five-Month Wait

*Jana Nayagan* was originally scheduled for a grand Pongal release on January 9. KVN Productions submitted the film to the Central Board of Film Certification on December 18, 2025. An initial examining committee recommended a U/A certificate. Then CBFC chairperson Prasoon Joshi referred the film to a Revising Committee after a complaint about its portrayal of religious sentiments and the armed forces.

The producers went to the Madras High Court, arguing the delay was causing massive financial strain. They eventually withdrew the case, choosing to wait for CBFC clearance through the standard process. That process has been ongoing for nearly half a year.

## The Piracy Blow

On April 9, the entire film leaked online in HD. It wasn't a cam print or a partial leak — the full movie was shared repeatedly across social media platforms. For a film that had already missed its theatrical window by three months, the piracy compounded the damage significantly. Reports indicate that the OTT deal, which had already been reduced after the postponement, was cut further following the leak.

## Why June 19

The June 19 date, if it holds, is strategic. It falls three days before Vijay's 52nd birthday on June 22 — a window that could turn the release into a fan celebration. There's also the question of KVN Productions' first Malayalam film, *Balan The Boy* (directed by the *Manjummel Boys* filmmaker Chidambaram), which is also scheduled for June 19. Whether both films release simultaneously from the same banner remains unclear.

Tamil Nadu's minister for film technology, Rajmohan, addressed the situation publicly this week: "The film can be released only after obtaining censor certification. We cannot do such things to any film for political reasons or any other reasons. The work for that is currently in progress."

## The NRI Angle

For the Tamil diaspora worldwide, *Jana Nayagan* represents something unprecedented — the final cinematic performance of an actor who left the industry to enter politics and won. Vijay's political journey from superstar to Chief Minister mirrors a trajectory that has captivated Tamil communities from Chennai to Toronto to Singapore to the Bay Area.

The film stars Bobby Deol as the antagonist, with Pooja Hegde and Mamitha Baiju in major roles. Anirudh Ravichander composed the music. H. Vinoth directed. It was made under KVN Productions with the kind of budget and ambition that was supposed to mark a superstar's grand farewell.

Instead, it became a case study in how censorship politics, piracy, and timing can conspire against even the most anticipated releases. Whether June 19 finally resolves that remains to be seen — but the fact that ticket platforms are listing dates before the producers are confirming them tells you something about the pressure building around this film.
author: Diaspora Desk
